additional_info.subject: 0399691 - ID0399691-DC/Si-D/IT - [u9YOAH] Session abort during cable check CRM:00314000135
additional_info.body:
Good evening colleagues,
I am writing you in regards of the topic of “charging sessions aborted during CableCheck” on
La Linea
project.
I analyzed the logs of several failed charging sessions over the last 24 hours on the #3 chargers affected at La Linea (chargers 170000810, 170000811, 170000812). You can find the results of the analysis in the attached Excel file. To summarize the symptoms:
At a first glance, it seems that the
charging sessions aborted during CableCheck
are caused by errors coming from the feedback of the Outgoing Contactors and the Switching Matrix Contactors.
For charger 170000810, the failed sessions seem to be caused by contactors QA21-22 and in one case QA11-12.
For charger 170000811, the failed sessions seem to be caused by contactors QA09-10 and QA21-22.
For charger 170000812, the failed sessions seem to be caused by contactors QA21-22.
After a careful analysis, however, I cannot exclude the possibility that the State Monitor KF13 of the chargers might be the cause of the failed sessions. As a matter of fact, in the logs we read the commands/feedback exchanged between PLC and State Monitor, but it is only the state monitor interacting directly with the contactors. Therefore, for the events involving the Outgoing Coils there might be the chance that the State Monitor does not send the commands to the contactors correctly.
Therefore, in order to have a speedy solution for the end customer, I suggest ordering and replacing both the contactors and the state monitors. In the meantime, I will escalate this topic to R&D, to determine if their analysis can identify the fault in one of the two components. However, this process might require more time.
As already communicated from the discussion with procurement, to support the claim to TDK, it is recommended to replace all contactors in the charger, once a faulty contactor is detected. The spare parts required are therefore:
8EM5903-0AA00-7AA8 - Contactor DC 2P 500A 1200VDC
8EM5903-0AA00-6AA1 - State Monitor 2x CCS, 1x AC, 1x CHAdeMO
Regarding the topic of “charging session aborted on both outlets during parallel charging”, at a first glance I didn't notice any event. A deeper analysis is required. My colleague @Sambath will carry on the analysis tomorrow and we will provide updates as soon as possible.
With kind regards,

additional_info.body:
Dear Team,
Hope you are doing well.
In reference to the failure of the charging session during parallel charging, I was able to examine the three chargers' logs for the previous seven days and discovered that certain sessions were interrupting with the parallel charging session. For your reference, a summary is provided below:
Analysis summary:
Sl.No
Charger ID
Timestamp
Event Summary
Suspected Root Cause
1
f6ZPFr
2025-01-08T09:23:11.000000
Charging was progressing with DC2, and a new charging session was initiated by DC1. DC1 failed charging session with contactor feedback error
[AbNormal(off FBK while on)].
Immediately after this DC2 session interrupted with "code":67,"msg":"ERR_EV_DROPPED, vehicle ended with unexpected pilot state B"}}
DC1 session failure - OGC or state monitor
DC2 session failure - State Monitor or EV
2
u9YOAH
2025-01-08T18:34:22.9994
Charging was progressing with DC1, and a new charging session was initiated by DC2. DC1 failed charging session with contactor feedback error
[AbNormal(off FBK while on)]
when DC2 change its state to C2.
DC2 also failed with
AbNormal(on FBK Timeout)
DC1 session failure - OGC or state monitor
DC2 session failure - OGC or state monitor
3
suBu8t
2025-01-08T18:34:22.9994
Charging was progressing with DC2, and a new charging session was initiated by DC1.  DC2 failed charging session with contactor feedback error
[AbNormal(off FBK while on)]
when DC2 change its state to C2. DC1 continue to deliver power.
DC2 session failure - OGC or state monitor SECC: no communication for 750ms
4
u9YOAH
2025-01-15T10:21:50.611759
Charging was progressing with DC2, and a new charging session was initiated by DC1.  SMC - MG1-MG2_QA09-10 stuck in ON feedback leading DC1 charging interruption & kept the outlet OoO till DC2 complete the charging ( Expected behavior )
DC1 session failure - SMC QA09-10 -
AbNormal(on FBK while off),
It is clear from the analysis that the failures were an aftereffect of contactor error or the state monitor fault. The findings are in line with Fosco’s analysis & point towards the contractor or state monitor fault.
Please feel free to contact me immediately if you observe any parallel charging failures.
Thanks & Regards,
Sambath.K.S

additional_info.subject: Re: 0399691 - ID0399691-DC/Si-D/IT - [u9YOAH] Session abort during cable check CRM:00314000135
additional_info.body:
Good morning Giuseppe,
I already quickly aligned with Luca this morning. To answer your doubt: no, there is no need to replace the contactors prepared for the dispenser (so contactor pairs QA19/20 and QA23/24)
These contactors are never operated, they are just commanded (together with the other contactors) during the “contactors' check” at the end of the converter grouping. However, since there is no dispenser and no plan to install a dispenser afterwards, there is no need to replace them. A possible error in their feedback will never affect the charger and the outlets DC1 and DC2.
I'm available for any further clarification.

additional_info.subject: Re: 0399691 - ID0399691-DC/Si-D/IT - [u9YOAH] Session abort during cable check CRM:00314000135
additional_info.body:
Good morning Giuseppe and Luca,
Last Friday I was informed that the Contactors and State Monitor were replaced on charger
170000812 (suBu8t).
This morning I had a look at the performance of the charger over the weekend, and this is the outcome from the monitoring activity:
The charger performed
24 charging sessions
between Friday (24.01.2025) after replacement and this morning (Monday 27.01.2025)
Only one event of QA21-22 non responding correctly on Saturday 2025-01-25T17:44:04 UTC. Issue did not appear anymore afterwards, with 3 successful charging sessions on DC1.
On 2025-01-24T20:50:31, an attempt to charge on DC1 failed. This event was caused by a Timeout of CableCheck (cable check lasted more than 38seconds). I checked the logs and the issue was probably caused by the fact that, as soon as DC1 was about to complete CableCheck, DC2 was plugged in as well, and a new power-alignment and converter relocation was triggered. This caused the cablecheck of DC1 to last more than the time allowed from the standards.
Please let me know when the contactors and state monitors will be replaced also on the chargers
170000810 and 170000811.
I will proceed then to monitor all 3 chargers.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: 0399691 - ID0399691-DC/Si-D/IT - [u9YOAH] Session abort during cable check CRM:00314000154
additional_info.body:
Ciao Luca,
As discussed today during the Taskforce alignment with PLM, we will proceed to close the Taskforce for La Linea, hence this ticket
ID0399691
and the old ticket
ID0007034.
The issue had been identified on some out-of-standard spikes coming from the Yutong Buses, resulting in the parallel disconnection of DC1 and, as consequence, in an idle-state of the CPPP.
The current workaround is to reboot the chargers.
Further communication to EcoG is maintained by CS as per established process.
EcoG will continue to recreate the CPPP stuck condition in their in-hour charger and provide feedback to Siemens.
Transparency to RC-IT on EcoG progresses will be maintained by ES.
No further in-site activities involving HQ are envisioned for this project.
The taskforce is considered closed and further updates will be shared according to EcoG progress on their internal investigation.
Thank you again for the collaboration and the support through all the activities!
With kind regards,
